prize_parts.citation: for the development of general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement prize for palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling to Buchwald and Hartwig. After the first round, no member disputes its maturity, its mechanistic understanding or the Buchwald and Hartwig pairing, and four of eight members place it in their configuration. On the chair's question about distinctness from 2010: the 2010 prize honored C-C bond formation through oxidative addition, transmetalation and C-C reductive elimination. C-N coupling needed a different solution, because amido-palladium complexes undergo competing beta-hydride elimination and reductive elimination from a heteroatom-bound metal is far harder. Bulky chelating and then dialkylbiarylphosphine and hindered NHC or trialkylphosphine ligands solved that specific problem, and that ligand design principle is what made the reaction general across amine and aryl-halide classes. It is a different elementary-step problem, not a broader scope for the same one. On Kosugi and Migita: their 1983 work used aryl halides with aminostannanes, which required stoichiometric toxic tin amides and had a narrow amine scope. The catalytic reaction with free amines and a base, which is what chemists now use, came from Buchwald's 1995 and Hartwig's 1995 to 1996 work, followed by the ligand generations that made it work on challenging substrates. I would cite the development of the general catalytic method and acknowledge Kosugi in the scientific background, not as a laureate. That keeps two names and a clean attribution.
statement.case_against: The honest weakness is that this is a second prize on palladium cross-coupling in sixteen years, and a member who weighs conceptual novelty above generality and use will see it as a method for one bond type. The Kosugi and Migita priority also cannot be waved away: the citation has to say 'general' and 'ligand-controlled' so that it does not claim the first aryl amination. Against the alternatives, targeted protein degradation offers a new design principle and modality but lacks an approved drug and has an unresolved PROTAC and cereblon glue credit split. Base editing is a decade old with safety data still accruing and, in my view, is protein engineering more than chemical reaction development.

responses.point: Linke proposes a two-part prize pairing B057 (Buchwald, Hartwig) with B058 base editing credited to Liu alone, to reflect the breadth of chemistry and to keep three people.
responses.response: I agree that B057 is the strongest and most mature part, and I accept your wording of its citation. I do not follow you on the pairing. A second part should not be added to broaden a prize; it should be added when it is itself a prize-level achievement with clean credit. B058 is about a decade old, its long-term safety record is still accruing, and the 2020 genome-editing prize is a recent predecessor. The chemical step is engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins, and you yourself note that Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments and that Nishida and Kondo worked independently. A Liu-only citation therefore makes a contested credit judgment to fit a three-person cap. I would sooner see B057 stand alone and let base editing mature than pair it now. If the committee wants a second part this year, I would look at B004 first, but only if its credit can be settled.

responses.point: Aili argues that targeted protein degradation is a new design principle, turning ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, and that maturity alone should not outweigh it.
responses.response: I take that argument seriously and have kept B004 as my first alternative. A designable rule of change the warhead and you change the target is exactly the kind of structure-to-function logic I value, and the VHL and cereblon ternary-complex structures give it real structural evidence. My difficulty is twofold. First, no degrader is approved, so the claim of changed practice rests on clinical-stage compounds rather than completed outcomes. Second, the cap of three names splits the field: Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli cover the PROTAC concept, but the thalidomide and cereblon glue discovery, which has the clearer clinical record, belongs to Handa and Ito and is left out. A citation that says induced proximity would cover both strands, but then the three names no longer match it. I do not regard B057's maturity as sufficient by itself, but with clean attribution and demonstrated use it is the better-prepared prize this year, and B004 can follow when a drug is approved.

responses.point: Aqvist lists the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize as the main objection to B057, and in his configuration keeps two names with the citation wording 'general ligand-controlled'.
responses.response: I agree that overlap is the real objection and we should answer it in the citation instead of ignoring it. My argument is that the 2010 prize rests on C-C coupling steps, while C-N coupling required solving amido-palladium reductive elimination and suppressing beta-hydride elimination, which was the ligand problem that kept the reaction from working for twenty years after Migita. Your phrase 'ligand-controlled' states that. I would keep the third slot empty rather than fill it, because adding Kosugi or any other name moves the citation toward a priority dispute that the 'general' wording already handles.

responses.point: Somfai holds that Pd C-N coupling is clearly new relative to 2010, that Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide work is a precursor, and that two names is clean.
responses.response: We agree on the substance, and your synthetic perspective is what I rely on for the practical point: the tin-free, catalytic reaction on free amines is the version that entered total and medicinal synthesis. That answers my own round-1 worry about whether the priority could justify a third name. I now judge it does not, provided the citation says 'general' and the committee text acknowledges Kosugi and Migita as precursors. I would ask you to say if you think a reader who knows the history would still object, because that is the only argument I still regard as open.

uncertainties: Whether a second cross-coupling-related prize within sixteen years will be read as too incremental, which the citation can reduce but not remove.
Whether the committee will accept the wording 'general' and 'ligand-controlled' as sufficient to handle the Kosugi and Migita precursor without naming them.
Whether B004 will become the better choice once an approved degrader exists, and how its PROTAC and glue credit would then be divided.
I rely on recalled literature for dates and scope in the Pd amination history and have not verified them in this exercise.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My Stockholm University affiliation is shared with Peter Brzezinski, whose first choice is B026, but this is a departmental relationship only and does not touch any candidate. No mentor, collaborator or institutional link to Buchwald, Hartwig, Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Liu or any other named candidate. Nothing in round 1 changed this disclosure.
